source_title: The Smithsonian raised $2.5 billion a year ahead of the schedule to fund museums, research and education; - The Times of India
source_excerpt: The Smithsonian Institution has raised $2.5 billion through its Campaign for Our Shared Future, reaching its fundraising target a full year ahead of schedule. Announced on 5 February 2026, the achievement marks the largest fundraising campaign in the history of a cultural organisation. Launched in 2018, the initiative brought together donors from across the United States and around the world to support the institutionâs museums, research centres, educational programmes and cultural projects. The milestone comes in 2026, the year the United States celebrates 250 years since the Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.The Smithsonian raised historic $2.5 billion ahead of scheduleAccording to the Smithsonian Institutionâs official news release, the Campaign for Our Shared Future attracted contributions from more than 730,000 donors across all 50 US states and 132 countries. Around 65% of those who contributed were first-time donors, highlighting the campaignâs ability to reach people who had not previously supported the institution financially.The campaign began in 2018, although it was publicly launched in September 2024. Its original target was to raise $2.5 billion by 2026, coinciding with the 250th anniversary of the signing of the US Declaration of Independence. Reaching the goal a year early gave the institution an opportunity to look ahead to its next phase of development.The Smithsonianâs February 2026 announcement described the achievement as a defining moment for the institution and the country it serves. The fundraising total also established a record for cultural organisations, placing the campaign among the largest philanthropic efforts ever undertaken in the museum and cultural sector.The Smithsonianâs fundraising effort was designed to support its work across a broad network of institutions rather than focus on a single museum or project. Its museums, research facilities, educational centres and cultural programmes serve different audiences, from visitors exploring American history to scientists studying the natural world.What will the campaign support across the institutionThe Smithsonianâs campaign website identifies 4 main priorities for the money raised: advancing sustainability and discovery, illuminating the nationâs past, opening pathways to new knowledge, and powering creativity and innovation.These priorities reflect the institutionâs wide-ranging responsibilities. Its work includes preserving historical objects, presenting exhibitions, conducting scientific research and making educational resources available to the public. The campaign is intended to strengthen these activities while helping the Smithsonian reach more people.The Smithsonianâs official announcement reported that the campaign had enabled 13 of its museums and centres to receive their largest gifts ever. The funds have supported exhibitions and programmes on the National Mall in Washington, DC, alongside partnerships and learning opportunities in communities across the country.Why was the fundraising target so significantAn earlier report published by Artnet News in September 2024 explained the scale of the campaign by comparing its $2.5 billion target with the Smithsonianâs annual budget, which was approximately $1.25 billion at the time. The fundraising goal was therefore equivalent to roughly two years of the institutionâs annual budget.The report also noted that the Smithsonianâs previous major fundraising campaign, launched in 2014, had sought $1.5 billion. The newer initiative set a substantially higher target, reflecting the institutionâs ambitions for its museums, research facilities and public programmes.The 2024 announcement placed the fundraising drive in the context of the approaching American semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.How does private support complement federal fundingThe Smithsonian operates through a combination of federal funding and private contributions. According to the institutionâs announcement, this public-private model has helped it expand what it can accomplish for the public.Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III said the achievement reflected the generosity of people across the country. The balance between these funding sources is important to the Smithsonianâs operations. Federal support provides a foundation for its public responsibilities, while donations can help advance additional projects, programmes and institutional priorities.Congress established the Smithsonian Institution in 1846 following a request from British scientist James Smithson, who left his fortune to establish an institution dedicated to the increase and diffusion of knowledge.That original gift helped create an institution whose work has grown considerably over nearly two centuries. The Smithsonian now describes itself as the worldâs largest museum, education and research complex, encompassing 21 museums, a zoo, research facilities, libraries, cultural centres and educational facilities.The fundraising achievement provides the Smithsonian with a significant foundation for its continuing work.
